## 43. PBD CORRECTION-vs-DRAFT DIFF CAPTURE — BUILT & VERIFIED (flywheel Phase 1, language side)
The highest-value training signal for the future local model: not just the corrected program, but WHAT the operator changed from the AI draft.
- New `programming_by_demonstration/correction_diff.py` — `compute_correction_diff(draft, corrected)` with robust step matching (stable id → action-aligned fallback), per-field deltas categorized pose/offset/speed/gripper/part/action/label/other, pose-list element-wise deltas (old/new/Δ), top-level diff (name/description/tags/config keys), reorder detection, summary block with `no_change`/`verbatim_accept`/`degraded`.
- `learning_store.py` — new `save_correction_diff(demo_id, ai_draft, corrected)` writes `correction_diff.json` + updates index; new `load_draft(demo_id)`; SQLite migration via ALTER TABLE for `poses_adjusted`/`steps_changed`/`verbatim_accept` (existing DBs upgrade in place); `stats()` now reports `diffs_present`, `verbatim_accept_rate`, `avg_poses_adjusted_per_demo`, `fields_changed_by_category`, `most_corrected_field_types`.
- `dashboard_server.py` — after `save_correction` in `/api/pbd/{demo_id}/correct`, loads the stored draft and calls `save_correction_diff` best-effort (failure logged, Accept never blocked); returns `diff_summary`.
- VERIFIED: schema migration applied to existing index.db; a hand-crafted draft+corrected pair produced correct per-step/field deltas (pose Δ [+0.02,0,+0.01...], offset_z_delta_mm=+20, speed −10, +1 step, −1 step); a verbatim accept → `no_change:true`/`verbatim_accept:true`; `stats()` reports the new aggregates. Backward compatible — older demos load and just lack a diff. Pure local code, no API dependency (works regardless of API key).
- NOTE flagged during this work: the dashboard's HTTP event loop has a pre-existing WEBSOCKET-RELATED STALL (unrelated to the diff change; verification was driven directly against LearningStore to route around it). Possibly behind the tab-staleness/lag symptoms — worth investigating separately.

## 45. PBD PALLET-GRID BUG — "1 by 1" wrong; structural gap (schema had no grid fields)
- Saying "place in a 1 by 1 pallet pattern" (or any grid) produced wrong geometry. ROOT CAUSE (confirmed in code): the intent schema `IntentOperation` had NO rows/cols/grid fields, the understanding system prompt never asked the model to extract grid dimensions, and `program_composer._build_palletize` never wrote `config.pallet`. So spoken grid info was DROPPED — heard but nowhere to go — and the executor expanded `move_to_pallet` against a default pallet.
- FIX prescribed: add rows/cols/layers/fill_order/spacing to the palletize intent schema (backward-compat wrap old plain strings); instruct the understanding prompt to EXTRACT the grid ("1 by 1"→1×1 single position, "3 by 4"→3×4, "2 rows of 5"→2×5, "row of 6"→1×6, layers/stacking) with few-shot examples and "don't silently guess material ambiguities"; have `_build_palletize` WRITE `config.pallet` so the executor + PalletConfigEditor use the spoken grid. "1 by 1" = exactly one placement is the canonical test case.

## 46. PBD INTERACTIVE CLARIFICATIONS — turn ambiguity into answerable questions
- Requirement: when speech/video is unclear, surface CLARIFYING QUESTIONS the operator answers (vs silently guessing). Existing infra: schema already has `ambiguities: List[str]` + `confidence_overall`; the wizard DISPLAYS them as a read-only amber list (passive, unanswerable).
- Prescribed upgrade: schema `ambiguities` → structured clarification objects {id, field (part/count/pallet_grid/location/speed/gripper/order), question, type (choice/number/text/part_select), options, suggested (best-guess default), affects (step/field)}; understanding prompt emits these with concrete options + suggested defaults; frontend REVIEW phase renders them as INTERACTIVE inputs (choice buttons / number / taught-parts dropdown / text) pre-filled with `suggested`, answering UPDATES the draft (e.g. pallet_grid→config.pallet, part→target_part_id); operator can Accept-with-defaults (defaults explicit, not hidden); answers recorded for the learning loop so the model needs fewer clarifications over time. Key design: suggested defaults shown, so ambiguity is surfaced WITHOUT turning every demo into an interrogation. Ties to §45 — an unsure grid becomes "1 by 1 / a row / a grid?" with "1 by 1" suggested.

## 47. DETECT STEP — part dropdown (taught parts only) + Teach-New entry point
- The detect step's old All/Library "Detection Mode" select was replaced with a "Detect Part" DROPDOWN listing ONLY taught library parts (GET /api/parts filtered to teach_count>0; untaught BT parts excluded); stores target_part_id + target_part_name on the step; detect action def fields ['mode']→['target_part']; step factory default target_part_id:null. A green "+ Teach New Part" button reuses the existing TeachWizard via a pendingTeachNew store flag (AdaptivePicking auto-opens it on mount, then clears the flag); returning to the Program tab refreshes the dropdown so the newly-taught part is selectable.
- HONEST EXECUTOR GAP (program_executor_node.py:631): the detect action is currently a 1-SECOND SLEEP PLACEHOLDER — it never read the old `mode` and does NOT yet read `target_part_id`. So the program JSON correctly carries the selected part, but the ROBOT does not yet honor it at runtime. To actually target the part, that `elif action == 'detect':` block must consume `target_part_id` and drive the matcher (then colcon --symlink-install + restart executor). Selection is currently a SPECIFICATION, not a runtime behavior.

## 49. CONTOURED STATIC KEEP-OUT ZONES — box→contour, and the box-fallback inconsistency
- User chose CONCAVE/CONTOURED zones (tightest visual) over OBB/convex. Built (markers `visual_mesh`, `capsule_to_hull_distance` confirmed on origin/main): outlier rejection before fitting (`remove_statistical_outlier` + 2nd-98th percentile clip), ALPHA-SHAPE concave mesh for VISUAL (alpha candidates 0.04→0.18, smallest non-empty wins = tightest), CONVEX HULL for COLLISION (`compute_convex_hull` + `capsule_to_hull_distance`), fallback chain alpha→hull→box, decimation for tablet. The split is deliberate: concave mesh for LOOKS, convex hull for the MATH (planners decompose concave anyway). 
- **Box-vs-contour inconsistency bug:** the viewer sometimes showed boxes, sometimes contours. ROOT CAUSE (CollisionOverlay ObjectBox ~line 159): a zone renders contoured ONLY if `obj.visual_mesh || obj.collision_hull` present; if BOTH missing it falls through to the box renderer. So zones whose alpha-shape failed (sparse clusters) or stale pre-contour zones show as boxes. FIX prescribed: static_zones must ALWAYS store at least a hull mesh per zone (alpha → hull → minimal-hull-from-OBB-corners, never no-mesh), and zones must be REBUILT (the recurring lesson). Point cloud occasionally appearing is FINE per user (leave it).
- (Earlier in the arc, the giant "0mm" floor box from v18 §29 was confirmed fixed via the max-size/footprint/flat-sheet rejections + ground-clearance cull; the contour work builds on that.)

## 51. DH-ACCURATE URDF FROM CAD — the path to a Standard-Bots-style movable model

### 51a. Current state
The 3D viewer machinery is DONE: URDFLoader, per-link decimated `_light.glb` meshes (tablet-safe), Z-up→Y-up handling, joint animation from WebSocket. The served URDF is `s10-140-provisional.urdf` (manual-derived approximations). User now HAS the DH data and the manuals. Next step = build a DH-ACCURATE URDF and serve it (dashboard /robot/urdf endpoint ~line 4143, swap provisional→accurate, keep provisional fallback).

### 51b. The zero-pose convention (from the manual, confirmed)
Estun controller APOS [0,0,0,0,0,0] = J1:0, J2:0, **J3:90°**, J4:0, **J5:90°**, J6:0 (Chinese readout 轴3:90.000, 轴5:90.000). So URDF needs −90° handling on J3/J5. RECOMMENDATION: handle the controller↔URDF offset in the DRIVER (add/subtract 90° on J3/J5), keep the URDF clean — build the assembly/URDF in the canonical URDF-zero pose. Base frame: Z+ up, connector (航插) points −Y (a real-world landmark for orientation / mirror checks).

### 51c. SolidWorks coordinate-system export method — DOCUMENTED
[DOCUMENT] `/mnt/user-data/outputs/SolidWorks_Joint_CS_to_URDF.md` — full procedure: place ONE coordinate system per joint IN THE ASSEMBLY, on the true rotation axis (Z = rotation axis, X = toward next joint, Y forced); each joint CS is the SHARED frame for the links on both sides (define once, not per-part — guarantees consecutive frames agree); the transform between consecutive joint frames IS the URDF joint origin (measure via Measure tool or a VBA macro dumping 4×4 transforms); export each link mesh RELATIVE TO ITS INPUT joint CS so meshes auto-align → `<visual><origin>` all zero and `<axis xyz="0 0 1"/>` uniform; CROSS-CHECK CAD-measured joint origins against the DH table (two independent sources agreeing = high confidence). 
- **Axis convention clarified across the session:** Z = the ROTATION AXIS (the line the joint spins about), NOT toward the next joint — critical because shoulder/elbow pitch joints spin about a SIDEWAYS axis perpendicular to the arm. +Z direction sets the positive-rotation SIGN (match the controller; a wrong guess is a one-line sign flip, fixable on arrival via jog-test). X direction within the perpendicular plane sets the ZERO reference (align to DH to avoid per-joint offsets). Y is forced (Z×X). Getting the AXIS right is structural; +Z direction and X are forgiving/fixable.
- A diagram was produced showing per-joint CS placement (J1 Z up, J2/J3 Z sideways = pitch axes, J4 Z along forearm, J5 Z sideways, J6 Z out the flange; J3/J5 flagged with the 90° zero offset).
- User has a proper DH/kinematic frame diagram (Link 0–5 with d[0], a[1], a[2], d[3], d[4], d[5] labeled, axis triads) — confirmed this IS the right format. Still need the NUMERIC values (or the full DH table a/α/d/θ-offset per joint) to author the exact URDF.

### 51d. The "auto-derive joints from the assembly" question — honest limits
- Cannot upload a SolidWorks assembly for Claude to derive joints: it's proprietary binary (needs SolidWorks/a CAD kernel); a STEP export gives geometry but NOT joint relationships (those live in the assembly MATES, which don't survive STEP); auto-inferring revolute joints from raw geometry is unreliable and would produce plausible-but-wrong kinematics. The full assembly GLB (229MB/294k tris) is too big and is visual-only anyway.
- **The tool that DOES auto-derive: the SW URDF Exporter plugin** — define joint coordinate systems + parent/child in the assembly, it exports URDF + aligned meshes in one shot. CAVEAT (recurring): incompatible with SolidWorks 2025. So: older SolidWorks (2021-2023) → plugin one-click path; SolidWorks 2025 only → coordinate-systems-in-assembly + manual transform read (macro + Python converter). User confirmed placing the coordinate systems IN THE ASSEMBLY is the right approach and asked which SW version gates the plugin — version TBD.

### 51e. How Standard Bots has a movable model — demystified
Not magic: they author the kinematic model by hand from authoritative design data (their own DH), export meshes joint-aligned at design time, and the controller does FK on live encoder values + renders — exactly what NeuRobots's dashboard already does (URDFLoader + WebSocket joint telemetry). Difference is vertical integration (their CAD team has the design truth internally); NeuRobots assembles the model from Estun's third-party data — same KIND of work, entirely doable, and validatable against the physical arm on arrival (pull joint values off the pendant). NeuRobots already has the hard parts (telemetry, renderer, FK, DH data); the one gap is the CAD→URDF assembly step (the §51c method).

### 51f. "Mate components in the viewer?" — possible but wrong tool
Building SolidWorks-style assembly mates into the Three.js viewer = weeks-to-months (raycasting + snapping + a constraint solver = reinventing a CAD kernel), and it solves a problem already solved in SolidWorks (the assembly is already mated). The viewer's job is to DISPLAY the model, not author it. The EASY, useful version = a lightweight joint-offset TUNER in the viewer (sliders to nudge each joint origin + the J3/J5 offset, live mesh-alignment verification) — adjustment of an already-loaded URDF, no solver. Recommended if the mesh-alignment step needs interactive polish.

## 54. VIDEO-UPLOAD 500 ERROR (PBD) — backend crash returning non-JSON
- PBD video upload fails: frontend shows "Generate error: Unexpected token 'I' ... 'Internal S'... is not valid JSON". DIAGNOSIS: that means the server returned PLAIN-TEXT "Internal Server Error" (HTTP 500), not JSON, and the frontend's `response.json()` choked. The real bug is a BACKEND CRASH during upload/generate; the JSON parse error is the symptom.
- Prescribed: read the actual traceback (`journalctl -u roboai-pbd` / `roboai-dashboard`); likely causes = ffmpeg failing on the uploaded video codec/container (phone .mov etc.), Whisper failing on extracted audio (no/empty audio track), temp-dir/disk/permissions on /opt/cobot/demonstrations/, or an uncaught exception in the generate handler. FIX both layers: (a) fix the actual crash AND wrap the endpoint to ALWAYS return JSON on error ({ok:false,error}), never bare text 500; (b) frontend tolerant of non-JSON (await res.text() fallback when not ok / not JSON) so it shows a readable message. Same lesson as the error boundaries — turn opaque failures legible. STATUS: prescribed, pending the traceback.

## 56. PROCESS LESSONS — JUNE 21-22 ADDITIONS (extend §41/§27/§13; all prior lessons govern)
19. **Get the ACTUAL error before fixing.** The Part Recognition crash was solved in one line ONCE the error boundary surfaced "useStore is not defined" — after an earlier wrong guess (extents/.toFixed) prescribed without the real error. Error text > theory. Insist on the console log / traceback / React error message first.
20. **Error boundaries turn opaque crashes legible.** Per-panel/per-tab boundaries converted blank white React death-screens into labeled "X failed to render — <message>" cards, which is what enabled fast fixes (cam0, parts). Adopt as standard per major tab. Same principle server-side: always return JSON-on-error so the frontend shows a real message, never a bare 500 (the video-upload bug).
21. **A render error boundary does NOT catch effect/handler/async errors.** If the global React error page shows instead of the boundary card, the throw is OUTSIDE render (effect/subscription/async) — guard there, don't keep adding render guards. (cam0 still-crashing diagnostic.)
22. **Structural gaps masquerade as model errors.** "1 by 1" pallet was wrong not because the model mis-heard but because the schema had NO field to hold the grid and the composer never wrote config.pallet — the info was dropped by plumbing. Check the data path end-to-end before blaming the model.
23. **A captured UI value is not a runtime behavior.** The detect-part dropdown saves target_part_id to the program JSON, but the executor's detect is a 1s sleep stub — selection is a SPECIFICATION until the executor consumes it. Verify the execution end honors UI selections, don't assume the JSON field does anything.
24. **Z = rotation axis, not "toward the next joint" (URDF frames).** The single most important CAD-to-URDF rule; pitch joints spin about a sideways axis. Get the axis exactly right (structural); +Z direction (sign) and X direction (zero ref) are forgiving/fixable. Two independent sources (CAD-measured + DH table) agreeing is the validation.
25. **Use the right tool for the layer.** Don't rebuild CAD mating in the Three.js viewer (weeks, reinvents a constraint solver, solves an already-solved problem); the viewer DISPLAYS, SolidWorks AUTHORS. The easy/useful viewer feature is a joint-offset tuner (adjust an existing URDF), not a mate solver.
